site_audit.platform: Hand-built static HTML (own /assets/css/style.css?v=5.5, /site.webmanifest, Google Fonts Outfit / DM Sans / Noto Sans Telugu). No CMS, no page builder, no plugin stack - the lightest build of the five.
site_audit.html_errors: 6 errors, 0 warnings, 0 info on the homepage - by far the cleanest of the five. The errors are 2 aria-label attributes on div elements without a role (the service carousel and the orbit stage), an output element inside a label whose id does not match the label's for attribute (the savings calculator's bill-out output), a role=tab with no corresponding role=tabpanel, a heading-level skip from h2 to h4, and a stray <script> start tag after </body> at source line 420.

issues: Your Search Console and Bing verification tokens are still the commented-out placeholders the developer shipped: the source carries <!-- <meta name="google-site-verification" content="PASTE_TOKEN"> --> and <!-- <meta name="msvalidate.01" content="PASTE_TOKEN"> -->. You are buying Google ads for a site Google has never been able to verify ownership of.

You run 1 live Google ad and the only tracking in your head is the Google Ads tag AW-609769092. There is no Meta Pixel, so nobody who leaves without filling the form can be reached again on Facebook or Instagram.

Your markup is the cleanest of the five - 6 errors, 0 warnings, 0 info - and your savings calculator publishes real numbers. That is the strongest asset in this audit and it is doing the work of five pages.
The checker finds a stray <script> start tag after </body> at source line 420, and your calculator's <output> element has an id that does not match the for attribute of its own label.
There is no live chat and no popup opt-in, so the quote form is the only capture point on the page.
No Meta Pixel installed — can't run retargeting or track ad conversions
No live chat — missing after-hours leads

promise_gap: Google Ads Transparency: 1 live ad under advertiser AR11194127933927063553, verified as CHITWALA JOHN SANDEEP - a sole proprietorship behind the Nature Power Solar trading name.

The ad buys a click to the best-built page in this audit: 6 errors, 0 warnings, 0 info, a live savings calculator with real Telangana tariffs, and JSON-LD that names the founder, the operations manager, the Google Maps listing and the exact subsidy tiers. The gap is not the page - it is that nothing on it is measured.

The site claims 'Authorised PM Surya Ghar vendor' and publishes the subsidy as ₹30,000 for 1 kW, ₹60,000 for 2 kW and ₹78,000 for 3 kW and above, plus ₹18,000 per kW for apartment societies up to 500 kW, with the scheme running to 31 March 2027.

Those figures match the published PM Surya Ghar schedule and the calculator's worked example (a ₹3,500 monthly bill resolving to a 4 kW system at ₹2.48 lakh, ₹78,000 subsidy, ₹1.7 lakh net, ₹3,325 a month saved, 4.1-year payback) is internally consistent. The claim is substantiated. What is missing is any way to see whether the claim converts.
The site claims '500+ installations' and '48-hour service - local team, every district'.

Neither figure is backed by a case study, a photograph or a review count on the page read in this pass, and the Search Console verification token is still a commented-out placeholder, so Google has never confirmed who owns the domain those claims sit on.

ads_audit.methodology: Control review follows the claude-ads Meta Ads audit catalog (github.com/vamsy16/claude-ads, ads/references/meta-audit.md). Each control is graded only where public evidence establishes it - Ad Library ad data and the lead's own landing page. Controls that require Ads Manager access (bidding, budgets, audiences, learning phase, EMQ, CAPI status) are marked unknown on purpose: they cannot be verified from outside the account and are never guessed.
